question: Will Renan Santos win the 2026 Brazilian presidential election?
description:
A presidential election is scheduled to take place in Brazil on October 4, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the listed candidate that wins this election.

This market includes any potential second round. If the result of this election isn't known by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Brazilian government, specifically the Superior Electoral Court (Tribunal Superior Eleitoral, TSE) (e.g., https://dadosabertos.tse.jus.br/).

eventMetadata.context_description: Lula da Silva maintains a lead in first-round polling around 39% to Flávio Bolsonaro’s 33%, with runoff simulations showing 47% to 43% as of late August 2026, aligning with trader pricing that places the incumbent at 62.5% implied probability. The Workers’ Party candidate benefits from incumbency, established voter base, and recent campaign launch events emphasizing social programs. Flávio Bolsonaro, nominated by the Liberal Party after his father Jair Bolsonaro’s ineligibility ruling, consolidates much of the right-wing vote but trails amid a fragmented field that includes Ronaldo Caiado, Romeu Zema, and Renan Santos in low single digits. Official campaigning began in mid-August, with polls indicating a likely runoff on October 25; recent Datafolha and other surveys show the gap stable within margins of error despite right-wing consolidation efforts.
